## Overview

This integration brings the trains of **Renfe**, the Spanish railway operator, into Gladys: the long and medium distance (AVE, Avlo, Alvia, Intercity, Regional, Avant…) and the **Cercanías** and **Rodalies** of every núcleo (Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, Sevilla, Bilbao…). It gives the **next trains, corrected in real time, with their delay**, at the stations you choose (three in the form, up to 10 more with a button), optionally towards a **destination station** (with the arrival time there) and for one **line**. The **track** of a Cercanías train is given once Renfe announces it. It also follows the **traffic** of up to six Cercanías lines (normal, traffic information, disrupted, heavily disrupted), with the alerts of Renfe: works, strikes, road replacement services. Each station and each line becomes a device to show on a dashboard and to use in scenes.

The data come from the **official open data of Renfe** (`data.renfe.com`), under the CC BY 4.0 licence: no account, no key. The two **timetables** (GTFS of the long distance and of the Cercanías) are downloaded only when Renfe publishes new ones, and kept by the integration. The **real time** (GTFS-RT) is read in **one request per network for every followed station**, every minute by default (every 10 minutes while no station announces anything in the next half hour, at night). The alerts are read every 5 minutes.

A train is **followed in real time** once it left its first station: its estimated time and its delay are given. Before that it is the **timetable**, marked "(timetable)". **Cancelled trains** and **stations not served** are shown.

This is a **cloud** integration: it contacts `ssl.renfe.com` (timetables) and `gtfsrt.renfe.com` (real time). Nothing else leaves your network.

## Requirements

- Gladys Assistant 5.3.0 or later.
- Nothing else: the open data of Renfe need no account and no key.

## Configuration

| Field                    | What to type                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Station 1, 2, 3          | The station as Renfe writes it: "Madrid-Atocha Cercanías", "Aranjuez", a part of it ("Chamartín") or its code. |
| Destination              | Only the trains calling afterwards at this station, with their arrival there. Empty: every train leaving.      |
| Line                     | Only this line: a Cercanías line ("C3", "R2N") or a long distance product ("AVE", "Avlo"). Empty: every line.  |
| Followed lines           | The Cercanías lines whose traffic you follow, six at most: "C3 Madrid, R2N".                                   |
| Reading of the real time | Every 30 seconds, minute, 2 minutes or 5 minutes.                                                              |
| Language of the texts    | Names of the devices, summaries and outputs of the scenes. Station names and traffic messages stay in Spanish. |

A station is one station of Adif, served by the long distance and the Cercanías alike: "Madrid-Atocha Cercanías" gives the C2 to C10 and the regional trains calling there; the high-speed trains leave from "Madrid-Puerta de Atocha-Almudena Grandes", another station. The **Find a station** button gives the stations holding a few words, with their code and their lines ("Madrid-Atocha Cercanías [18000] → Regional, C3 Madrid…"). A few words are enough when only one station holds them ("chamartin").

A Cercanías line is written with its núcleo when its name exists elsewhere ("C1" runs in ten núcleos): "C3 Madrid", "C1 Sevilla", "Rodalies R2"; alone, it is the one calling at your stations. **Test the connection** asks for the timetables again and reads each station and each line right away.

More stations than the three of the form (home, work, a weekly trip…): **Add a station** takes the same three fields — station, destination, line — and follows up to 10 more stations. **List the stations** shows every followed station, numbered; **Remove a station** takes that number (or the name). The added stations are kept in the configuration of Gladys, so they follow its backups.

The timetable of the Cercanías is a big file: the first reading, and the one of each new file, takes some 10 to 30 seconds.

## Usage

### Devices

In the **Discover** tab, create the devices you want:

- **Renfe \<station\> → \<destination\>**: the next train as text ("C3 → Aranjuez · 3 min (+2 min late) · track 2 · arr. 23:13", "AVE 3063 → Barcelona-Sants · 06:27 (timetable)"), the wait of the next train and of the one after (minutes), and the delay of the next one (minutes, published only when it is followed in real time);
- **Renfe Cercanías Madrid C3**, **Renfe Rodalies R2N**…: the traffic as text ("Disrupted traffic: Por obras de mejora…") and the number of traffic messages under way.

Without a train in the next four hours, the device shows the first one of each route in the next 24 hours.

### Traffic

Renfe publishes **alerts** for the Cercanías: a Spanish text, the lines concerned and their periods. The state of a line comes from its heaviest alert under way: **heavily disrupted** for an interruption or a road replacement service, **disrupted** for works, a strike, delays, modified frequencies, **traffic information** otherwise (lifts out of order, tickets); **normal** without an alert. An alert starting in the next three days is shown as coming. The alerts about a station only (a lift, an entrance) are left out. The long distance has no alerts: its delays and cancellations are those of the trains.

### Dashboard widgets

![The Renfe departures widget at Madrid-Chamartín and the Renfe traffic widget of Cercanías lines of Madrid (generated illustration, not a screenshot)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/William-De71/gladys-renfe/main/docs/assets/widgets.en.png)

- **Renfe departures**: the next trains of a station, compact. One row per line and destination, with its next trains in a row ("8 · 52 min"). A cancelled train is shown ("cancelled 22:35") and turns the row orange, like a delay of 5 minutes or more. The **Routes shown** setting sets the number of rows. Choose a followed station, or type any station (and a line) in the widget settings. With **Several stations**, one widget shows several station devices: the devices of one station are merged under its name; for different stations, each opens with a row of its own.
- **Renfe traffic**: the state of each line, then the alerts under way and those of the next three days, with their period. Tap a card for the full text. The followed lines, the ones typed in the settings, or the Cercanías lines of your stations when you follow none.

### Scenes

Triggers, once per change (the first reading is only a baseline):

- **Renfe: departure soon**: a train of a followed station leaves in 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20 or 30 minutes, counted on its real-time estimate.
- **Renfe: train late**: a train of a followed station leaving within two hours is 5, 10, 15, 30 or 60 minutes late or more, once per train and threshold.
- **Renfe: train cancelled**: a train of a followed station leaving within two hours is cancelled, or does not stop there any more.
- **Renfe: line disrupted**: a followed line becomes disrupted or heavily disrupted.
- **Renfe: back to normal**: no disruption under way on the line any more.
- **Renfe: new traffic message**: Renfe publishes an alert about a followed line, under way or coming.

Each gives a ready-made sentence, `{{triggerEvent.data.summary}}`, and its values (line, train number, destination, time, delay, track, title, text, start and end…). The actions **Renfe: next trains** and **Renfe: traffic of a line** return the same kind of values, to put in a message or to test in a condition.

Examples:

- When your C3 to Aranjuez leaves in 10 minutes → turn the hall lamp green.
- When your AVE to Barcelona is 15 minutes late or cancelled → send the summary to your phone before you leave.
- Every weekday at 7:30 → read the next trains of your station and have the kitchen speaker announce them.

### Transport

Cloud only: the data come from the internet. The timetables when Renfe publishes new ones, the real time of the networks of your stations in one request each, the alerts every 5 minutes.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Unknown or ambiguous"**: use **Find a station**, then copy the exact name or the code in brackets; for a Cercanías line, add its núcleo ("C1 Sevilla").
- **"(timetable)" after a train**: it has not left its first station yet, or Renfe does not follow it; the time is the one of the timetable.
- **No train towards the destination**: the destination must be a station the trains call at after yours; check the name with **Find a station**, or empty the destination to see every train.
- **A strike, many cancelled trains**: Renfe announces the cancellations of the day; they are shown for the next six hours, never for the following days.
- **"The open data of Renfe do not answer"**: the integration tries again at each reading; meanwhile the trains come from the timetables kept, and a reading of less than 3 minutes stands in for a refused one.
- **To report a problem**: press **Diagnostic**, then copy the lines starting with "Renfe diagnostic" from the Logs tab into a GitHub issue or a reply on the forum, with the versions of Gladys and of the integration.

## How to install Renfe in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Renfe appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/william-de71/gladys-renfe:0.1.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-renfe](https://github.com/William-De71/gladys-renfe).

Renfe requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Renfe is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [William-De71](https://github.com/William-De71), not by the Gladys core team.
